tools.description: Create a new .mstudio package on disk with an empty timeline. Initial tempo/timeSig/key are set by follow-up project.setTempo/setTimeSig/setKey commands so those mutations are uniformly journaled.

name.description: Display name for the new project; also the .mstudio package's name on disk. Non-empty. This is a NAME, not a path — project.open is the one that takes a path.

tools.name: studio_project_new

tools.description: Open an existing .mstudio package: read project.json (checkpoint), replay any journal segment newer than the checkpoint, and hydrate the in-memory model.

path.description: Filesystem path to an existing .mstudio package directory. Non-empty, and the package must already exist: this command never creates one.

tools.name: studio_project_open

tools.description: Write project.json as a checkpoint of the current journal tip and mark prior journal segments eligible for truncation once the write is durable.
tools.name: studio_project_save

tools.description: Set the project's global tempo in beats per minute. v1 has one tempo for the whole project (no tempo map / tempo automation).

bpm.description: Tempo in beats per minute, greater than 0 and at most 999. Journaled as a Num, so the integer/float SHAPE is part of the hash chain: send 120, not 120.0, unless you mean a fractional tempo.

tools.name: studio_project_set_tempo

tools.description: Set the bar length the grid, ruler and metronome count in, e.g. 4/4 or 6/8. One signature for the whole project in v1 — there is no signature map.

denominator.description: Beat unit — the BOTTOM number of 4/4 — one of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32.

numerator.description: Beats per bar — the TOP number of 4/4 — from 1 to 32.

tools.name: studio_project_set_time_sig

tools.description: Set the project's key/scale metadata (informational for v1; not enforced against note content).

key.description: Key and scale as '<root> <mode>', e.g. 'C major' or 'A minor'. Root is A-G with an optional '#' or 'b'; mode is 'major' or 'minor'. Matches the keyscale vocabulary ace_generator.py already uses. Metadata only — note content is not checked against it.

tools.name: studio_project_set_key

tools.description: Create or update a named arrangement section marker. Catalog default inverse is section.remove (correct for the create case); when section.set updates an EXISTING sectionId's fields, the runtime executor uses a self-inverse (section.set with the prior name/startTicks/color) instead. See engine/contracts/README.md open question: this is an upsert command with a context-dependent inverse, which a static per-command inverseRule cannot fully express.

color.description: Optional swatch, '#RRGGBB' hex with six digits and no alpha (e.g. '#FF8800'). Omitted leaves the section with no explicit colour.

name.description: Section label shown in the arrangement ruler, e.g. 'Verse', 'Chorus', 'Bridge' or 'Drop'. Non-empty.

sectionId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the section; the engine never mints one. A fresh id CREATES a section, an existing id UPDATES it (this command is an upsert).

startTicks.description: Where the section begins, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

tools.name: studio_section_set

tools.description: Delete an arrangement section marker. Only the label goes — no audio, clip or track is touched.

sectionId.description: Id of an existing section. Removing an id that is not there is a typed error, not a silent no-op.

tools.name: studio_section_remove

tools.description: Create or update a timeline marker. Catalog default inverse is marker.remove (correct for the create case; P0-C proposal 1, APPROVED by the coordinating session 2026-07-11, mirroring section.set/section.remove); when marker.set updates an EXISTING markerId's fields, the runtime executor uses a self-inverse (marker.set with the prior positionTicks/label/color) instead, the same upsert nuance as section.set.

color.description: Optional swatch, '#RRGGBB' hex with six digits and no alpha (e.g. '#FF8800'). Omitted leaves the marker with no explicit colour.

label.description: Text drawn on the marker in the ruler, e.g. 'Solo starts'. Non-empty.

markerId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the marker; the engine never mints one. A fresh id CREATES a marker, an existing id UPDATES it (this command is an upsert).

positionTicks.description: Marker position, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

tools.name: studio_marker_set

tools.description: Remove a timeline marker. Added as marker.set's undo-completing counterpart (P0-C proposal 1, APPROVED by the coordinating session 2026-07-11), mirroring section.remove.

markerId.description: Id of an existing marker. Removing an id that is not there is a typed error, not a silent no-op.

tools.name: studio_marker_remove

tools.description: Start playback from the current transport position. Unjournaled per 02-ARCH section 4: transport commands are real commands on the bus but never appear in journal.jsonl.
tools.name: studio_transport_play

tools.description: Stop playback and leave the playhead exactly where it stopped. Use transport.seek afterwards to move it. Unjournaled per 02-ARCH section 4.
tools.name: studio_transport_stop

tools.description: Jump the playhead to a position without starting or stopping playback. Unjournaled per 02-ARCH section 4.

positionTicks.description: Where to put the playhead, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Seeking past the end of the material is allowed.

tools.name: studio_transport_seek

tools.description: Mark the region the transport should loop over. Start must be strictly before end, so a zero-length loop cannot be set. Unjournaled view/transport state.

endTicks.description: Loop end, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Must be strictly AFTER startTicks.

startTicks.description: Loop start, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Must be strictly BEFORE endTicks; equal or inverted is refused, so a zero-length loop cannot be set.

tools.name: studio_transport_loop_set

tools.description: Turn looping off and leave the transport playing straight through. Unjournaled view/transport state.
tools.name: studio_transport_loop_clear

tools.description: Toggle the metronome click. v1 metronome is a simple click, no accent patterns or sound choices.

enabled.description: true starts the click, false stops it. Absolute, not a toggle: sending true twice leaves the click on.

tools.name: studio_transport_metronome

tools.description: Create an empty track to put clips, an instrument or effects on. The id is yours to mint and is permanent; index optionally places it in the list, otherwise it is appended.

index.description: Optional 0-based insert position; 0 makes it the first track. May equal the current track count (append), and anything larger is refused. Omitted appends.

name.description: Display name on the track header, e.g. 'Lead Vocal'. Non-empty, need not be unique, and is NOT the identity — trackId is.

trackId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the new track; the engine never mints one, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model. An id already in use is refused, never merged.

tools.name: studio_track_add

tools.description: Delete a track along with every clip, device, effect, send and automation lane on it. Undo restores all of it, so this is reversible; the audio assets under audio/ are content-addressed and are not deleted.

confirm.description: Must be true. This tool deletes project content or writes/publishes outside the project.

trackId.description: Id of the track to delete. Every clip, device, effect, send and automation lane on it goes too, and undo restores all of them.

tools.name: studio_track_remove

tools.description: Change the display name a person sees on a track header. The trackId is unaffected: ids are the wire identity and never change, so every clip, lane and binding that names this track keeps working.

name.description: New display name for the track. Non-empty.

trackId.description: Id of the track to rename. The id itself never changes — it is the wire identity for the life of the project.

tools.name: studio_track_rename

tools.description: Move a track to a different slot in the track list. Display order only: it changes nothing about routing or the mix.

newIndex.description: 0-based destination slot. Must be strictly LESS than the current track count — unlike track.add's index, which may equal it.

trackId.description: Id of the track to move.

tools.name: studio_track_reorder

tools.description: Give a track a colour in the timeline and mixer, so an arrangement can be read at a glance. Display only — it changes nothing about the audio.

color.description: Track colour as '#RRGGBB' hex: six hex digits, leading '#' required, no alpha channel (e.g. '#3AA6FF').

trackId.description: Id of the track being recoloured.

tools.name: studio_track_set_color

tools.description: Set how tall a track's lane is drawn in the timeline, e.g. to give the one you are editing more room. Display only.

heightPx.description: Lane height in points, 24 to 400. Purely how tall the lane is drawn; it changes nothing about the audio.

trackId.description: Id of the track whose lane height changes.

tools.name: studio_track_set_height

tools.description: Silence a whole track, or bring it back. Absolute rather than a toggle, so it is safe to send the same value twice; the state is journaled and undoable, and it is honoured by playback and by the master bounce.

muted.description: true silences the track in playback and in every bounce, false unmutes it. Absolute, not a toggle.

trackId.description: Id of the track to mute or unmute.

tools.name: studio_track_mute

tools.description: Hear one track (or a set of them) on its own by silencing everything not soloed. Honoured by playback and the master bounce, and deliberately IGNORED by stem export, which always writes every track.

soloed.description: true solos the track (only soloed tracks are heard), false unsolos. Absolute, not a toggle. Honoured by the master bounce and deliberately IGNORED by stem export, which always writes every track.

trackId.description: Id of the track to solo or unsolo.

tools.name: studio_track_solo

tools.description: Arm or disarm a track for recording. The armed track is the capture target for record.start; arming is journaled and undoable. Arming does not open the microphone — that happens at record.start (or opt-in record.inputListen).

armed.description: true arms the track for recording, false disarms. Absolute, not a toggle. Arming alone never opens the microphone — record.start or record.inputListen does.

trackId.description: Id of the track to arm. record.start captures onto armed tracks.

tools.name: studio_track_arm

tools.description: Choose which hardware input channel an audio track records from. On a four-input interface (e.g. Zoom AMS-44), set track 1 to channel 0, track 2 to channel 1, and so on, arm all four, and record once — each track lands its own channel. Journaled and undoable.

channel.description: 0-based hardware input channel this track records from: channel 0 is the first input on the interface. On a four-input box, set 0, 1, 2, 3 across four armed tracks and one pass lands each channel on its own track.

trackId.description: Id of the audio track whose hardware input assignment changes.

tools.name: studio_track_set_input_channel

tools.description: Add an instrument to a track. Its parameters become automatable IMMEDIATELY through the existing ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> — no contract change, which is what E0 3 promised. A NEW command name (E0 9.2).

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

kind.description: Which instrument to build: 'synth' (the four-waveform subtractive synth), 'sampler' (pitched, zone-mapped audio) or 'drum' (one pad per key). The E2 instrument vocabulary, and CLOSED — an unknown kind fails at the contract boundary.

trackId.description: Id of the track that will host the instrument. Give a track only ONE device: a second device is accepted here (only a duplicate deviceId is refused) but the render compile then hard-errors, because the baked note lane is per track and a second instrument would have no notes to play.

tools.name: studio_device_add

tools.description: Remove an instrument from a track. Refused if the device carries stored parameters this build has no command to restore, so removing it is always undoable.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

trackId.description: Id of the track the instrument sits on.

tools.name: studio_device_remove

tools.description: Bind an audio source to a sampler zone or a drum pad. This is what makes kind 'sampler' and kind 'drum' reachable at all: Device.params is Num-only and could never name an asset. A NEW command name (E0 9.2) — device.add is deliberately NOT widened with an optional sourceId, because replay does not validate params and an older binary would verify the chain and then silently build a sampler with no audio.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

gainDb.description: Optional zone/pad gain in dB. Default 0, which is unity.

hiPitch.description: Highest MIDI key the zone covers, 0 to 127. Must be >= loPitch, and must EQUAL loPitch on a 'drum' device, because a pad is one key.

loPitch.description: Lowest MIDI key the zone covers, 0 to 127.

pan.description: Optional pad pan, -1 is hard left and 1 is hard right; default 0 is centre. Honoured by kind 'drum'; IGNORED by 'sampler', which is a pitched instrument sitting on the track's own pan.

rootPitch.description: The MIDI note the recording sounds at, 0 to 127; a sampler reads at 2^((pitch-rootPitch)/12). Ignored by kind 'drum', which does not pitch-track.

sourceId.description: Content-addressed asset id — the SAME registry clip.place's assetHash names. Resolved render-side through the same loaded-source map, with the same loud 'references unloaded source' failure.

trackId.description: Id of the track the sampler/drum device sits on.

zoneId.description: Opaque, stable zone id. Identity for edit and undo.

tools.name: studio_device_zone_add

tools.description: Remove one source binding from a sampler or drum device. The inverse carries every field the zone held, gain and pan included, so remove+add is exact. Refused if the zone carries unknown fields this build has no command to restore. There is no device.zone.set: an edit is remove+add, which keeps every inverse exact without inventing per-field defaults.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

trackId.description: Id of the track the sampler/drum device sits on.

tools.name: studio_device_zone_remove

tools.description: Set one instrument parameter — the waveform an oscillator runs, its filter cutoff, its ADSR envelope. This is the setter E1/E2 deliberately omitted ("its inverse cannot be exact without per-parameter defaults that the DSP lane owns"); E5 answered that for fx.param.set and this is the same answer for Device: parameters stay SPARSE, an absent key means the DSP default exactly as build_instrument already implements it, so the inverse of setting an ABSENT key is device.param.clear and no default is ever materialized into the project. inverseShape is 'multi' because the declared inverse name cannot cover both directions. A NEW command name (E0 9.2) — device.add is deliberately NOT widened with optional params, because replay does not validate params and an older binary would verify the chain and then silently build an instrument with a different sound.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

key.description: An instrument parameter key from DEVICE_PARAM_KEYS — the SAME token the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> already carries, so a value authored here and a lane automating it name the parameter identically. Which keys a given kind honours is deliberately NOT validated: apply.rs runs on replay, so tightening the (kind, key) pairing later would break replay of a project that authored a key its kind ignores (a drum rack ignores 'waveform'; every kind but 'synth' ignores it).

trackId.description: Id of the track the instrument sits on.

value.description: Parameter value. Journaled as a Num, so the integer/float SHAPE round-trips exactly.

tools.name: studio_device_param_set

tools.description: Drop one stored instrument parameter, restoring sparsity so the key reads as the DSP default again. Clearing a key that stores no value is a typed error, not a silent no-op: a no-op has no exact inverse to journal.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

key.description: An instrument parameter key from DEVICE_PARAM_KEYS — the SAME token the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> already carries, so a value authored here and a lane automating it name the parameter identically. Which keys a given kind honours is deliberately NOT validated: apply.rs runs on replay, so tightening the (kind, key) pairing later would break replay of a project that authored a key its kind ignores (a drum rack ignores 'waveform'; every kind but 'synth' ignores it).

trackId.description: Id of the track the instrument sits on.

tools.name: studio_device_param_clear

tools.description: Begin capturing from an audio input onto an armed track. The host reports captureOriginTicks and rolling from the actual input-ready transport clock; while rolling, an omitted startTicks records at the live playhead and a supplied startTicks is ignored unless punchOutTicks defines a punch region. Opens an INPUT-only stream and never an output stream; monitoring stays silent. Unjournaled transport-class action: the take and clip landed by record.stop are the journaled, undoable unit.

deviceId.description: Optional input device name to open. Omitted opens the system default input.

punchOutTicks.description: Punch-out position. When set, record.stop lands a clip of exactly punchOutTicks minus startTicks (the punch region), truncating or silence-padding the capture to fit. Omitted means open-ended capture until record.stop.

startTicks.description: With punchOutTicks, the punch-in position. Otherwise, when stopped, the position where the take lands after snapping to the anchored bar grid; while rolling without a punch it is ignored. Default: the capture origin.

trackId.description: The armed track to capture onto.

tools.name: studio_record_start

tools.description: Complete the current loop-record pass without stopping or reopening the input stream. The host rotates the writer-side capture accumulator, immediately continues filling the next pass, and prepares the completed pass asynchronously before committing its atomic record transaction. No-op when nothing is recording.
tools.name: studio_record_rotate

tools.description: Stop the active capture and land the recorded audio as a candidate take and a placed clip with human-origin lineage (txn.begin / gen.landed sourceCommand record.commit / clip.place / txn.commit). No-op when nothing is recording.
tools.name: studio_record_stop

tools.description: Discard the active capture without landing a take or clip. No-op when nothing is recording.
tools.name: studio_record_cancel

tools.description: Opt-in input listen for gain-staging and per-channel metering WITHOUT recording. Arming a track never opens the mic; this command (or record.start) does. The snapshot reports inputOpen so the UI can show when an input is live. Monitoring (hearing yourself through speakers) stays double-gated and is not enabled by this command.

deviceId.description: Optional input device name to open. Omitted opens the system default input.

enabled.description: true opens the input for metering only (no landing); false closes it. Does not enable speaker monitoring.

tools.name: studio_record_input_listen

tools.description: Pin a specific control map to a MIDI input port, or hand it back to auto-detect. Reach for this when a controller is being matched to the wrong map.

device.description: Reported port name, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'.

map.description: Optional map key (file stem or map name) to pin to this port, 'none' to leave the port unmapped, or 'auto' to go back to pattern auto-detect. Omitted leaves the current selection alone.

tools.name: studio_midi_device_select

tools.description: Set what a MIDI input port's KEYS do: play the instrument (default) or drive its control bindings.

port.description: Reported port name, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'.

role.description: instrument (the DEFAULT): note messages play the selected instrument track and are recordable; the port's note-matched control bindings are suppressed, while its CC/pitch-bend bindings still fire. control: every binding fires and notes never sound.

tools.name: studio_midi_port_role_set

tools.description: Begin listening for the next control a person touches, so the following midi.binding.set can bind it without anyone having to know its channel and CC number.

device.description: Optional port name to scope capture to, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'. Omitted takes the first control from any device.

tools.name: studio_midi_learn_start

tools.description: Stop listening for a control. Any binding the session produced stays: it is undone with midi.binding.clear, not by closing the session.
tools.name: studio_midi_learn_stop

tools.description: Bind a physical knob, pad or key to a Studio action and persist it, so a controller can drive commands. Usually issued right after midi.learn.start captures the control.

control.description: Optional explicit control coordinates (type, channel, and number for note/CC). Omitted uses the learn session's captured control.

channel.description: MIDI channel to match, 0-BASED: 0 to 15. Channel 1 on the hardware is 0 here.

number.description: Note or CC number to match, 0 to 127. Optional, and omitted for pitchBend, which is channel-wide.

type.description: Which MIDI message class the binding matches: 'noteOn', 'noteOff', 'controlChange' or 'pitchBend'.

device.description: Optional port name whose resolved map takes the binding. Omitted uses the learn session's captured device.

enabled.description: Whether the binding fires at all. Default true; false keeps it on file without it acting.

label.description: Optional human-readable name for the binding, shown in MIDI settings. Omitted leaves it unlabelled.

target.description: What firing this control DOES. kind 'command' submits a catalog command (name + a params template that may carry the '$value' and '$track:N' placeholders), 'builtin' runs a named built-in action, 'sterling' queues instruction text for the Sterling copilot.

instruction.description: Instruction text queued for the Sterling copilot. Required for kind 'sterling', optional and ignored otherwise.

kind.description: Which target family this is: 'command' (a catalog command by name), 'builtin' (a named built-in action) or 'sterling' (instruction text queued for the copilot).

name.description: The action to run: with kind 'command' a catalog command name, with kind 'builtin' one of the built-in action names. Optional for kind 'sterling', which uses instruction instead.

params.description: Optional params template for kind 'command'. May carry the '$value' placeholder (the mapped control value) and '$track:N' (the Nth track's id).

valueMap.description: Optional scaling from the controller's raw reading to the value the target receives. Omitted, the raw is normalized to 0..1 and handed over as-is.

curve.description: How input maps onto output between the two ends: 'linear', 'exponential' or 'logarithmic'. Default 'linear'.

inputMax.description: Raw controller value treated as the high end, 0 to 127. Default 127.

inputMin.description: Raw controller value treated as the low end, 0 to 127. Default 0.

outputMax.description: Value produced at inputMax, in the TARGET parameter's own units. Default 1.

outputMin.description: Value produced at inputMin, in the TARGET parameter's own units (dB for a gain, -1..1 for a pan). Default 0.

tools.name: studio_midi_binding_set

tools.description: Drop one binding from a port's user overlay map, so that control goes back to doing nothing (or to whatever the bundled map says).

control.description: The exact control coordinates of the binding to drop — the same type/channel/number shape midi.binding.set matched on. There are no wildcards: a binding is cleared by naming it exactly.

channel.description: MIDI channel the binding matched, 0-BASED: 0 to 15.

number.description: Note or CC number the binding matched, 0 to 127. Omitted for pitchBend, which is channel-wide.

type.description: Which MIDI message class the binding matched: 'noteOn', 'noteOff', 'controlChange' or 'pitchBend'.

device.description: Reported MIDI port name whose user overlay map holds the binding, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'.

tools.name: studio_midi_binding_clear

tools.description: Copy a MIDI map file someone else wrote into the user maps directory so this install can resolve ports against it. The file is copied, not linked.

overwrite.description: Optional. true replaces an existing user map with the same file name; false (the default) refuses rather than clobbering it.

sourcePath.description: Filesystem path of the MIDI map file to bring in. It is COPIED into the user maps directory, so later edits to the original have no effect.

tools.name: studio_midi_map_import

tools.description: Write a MIDI map out verbatim to a path of your choosing, e.g. to share it or check it into a repository. Manage tier because it writes outside the app's directories.

confirm.description: Must be true. This tool deletes project content or writes/publishes outside the project.

map.description: Map key (file stem or map name).

outputPath.description: Filesystem path to write the map file to. Manage tier: this writes outside the app's own directories, so the tool also needs confirm: true.

tools.name: studio_midi_map_export

tools.description: Re-read every bundled and user MIDI map from disk and re-resolve the connected ports against them — what to call after editing a map file by hand.
tools.name: studio_midi_reload

tools.description: Put an existing content-addressed audio asset on a track as a clip. The asset must already be in the package (import.audio is what brings one in); clips on a track may not overlap.

assetHash.description: blake3 hash of the audio asset under audio/: 64 lowercase hex characters. The asset must already be in the package — this command references, it does not import.

clipId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the new clip; the engine never mints one. Must not already be in use anywhere in the project.

lengthTicks.description: How long the clip is, in ticks. The schema admits 0 for historical reasons but the executor REFUSES it: this must be greater than 0.

sourceOffsetTicks.description: Optional offset INTO the asset at which the clip starts reading, in ticks. Default 0 (play from the top of the file). offset + length must stay inside the asset's extent.

startTicks.description: Where the clip starts on the timeline, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

trackId.description: Id of the track to place the clip on. Clips on one track may NOT overlap — an overlapping placement is refused, not nudged.

tools.name: studio_clip_place

tools.description: Place an empty NOTE-BACKED (MIDI) clip on a track. A NEW command name, not an optional param on clip.place: catalog v2 design 9.2 — replay does not validate params, so an older binary would verify the chain and silently build a wrong model, whereas an unknown command name hard-fails the open.

clipId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the new note clip; the engine never mints one. Must not already be in use anywhere in the project.

lengthTicks.description: How long the clip is, in ticks; must be greater than 0. Note positions are CLIP-RELATIVE, so this is the window they live in.

startTicks.description: Where the clip starts on the timeline, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

trackId.description: Id of the track to place the clip on. Clips on one track may NOT overlap — an overlapping placement is refused.

tools.name: studio_clip_place_midi

tools.description: Move a clip to a new start position, optionally onto a different track. This is the exact command shown as the worked example in 02-ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.

clipId.description: Id of the clip to move.

startTicks.description: New clip start, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). The destination must be clear — clips on one track may not overlap.

trackId.description: Destination track; equal to the clip's current track for a same-lane move.

tools.name: studio_clip_move

tools.description: Move one edge of a clip to crop or extend it, without moving the audio inside it. Delta-based and self-inverse. The start edge is refused on a note-backed clip.

clipId.description: Id of the clip to trim.

deltaTicks.description: Signed tick delta, and it may not be 0. On the 'start' edge a positive value shortens from the front (the start moves later); on the 'end' edge a positive value lengthens. The result must leave a length greater than 0 and must not collide with a neighbouring clip.

edge.description: Which edge moves: 'start' or 'end'. 'start' is REFUSED on a note-backed clip (it would shift every note relative to the clip); 'end' works on audio and note clips alike.

tools.name: studio_clip_trim

tools.description: Cut one clip into two at a point strictly inside it. The left piece keeps the original id, the right piece takes newClipId, and no audio is re-encoded.

atTicks.description: Split point, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar), STRICTLY inside the clip: after its start and before its end. A split exactly on an edge is refused rather than silently ignored.

clipId.description: Id of the clip to split. It becomes the LEFT piece and keeps this id; the right piece gets newClipId.

newClipId.description: Caller-minted id for the RIGHT-hand piece the split creates; must not already be in use. The left piece keeps the original clipId.

tools.name: studio_clip_split

tools.description: Copy a clip and place the copy at another position on the SAME track — despite what earlier wording implied, this command carries no destination track and cannot move a copy to another lane. Use clip.duplicate then clip.move for that.

clipId.description: Id of the clip to copy. The original is untouched.

newClipId.description: Caller-minted id for the copy; must not already be in use.

startTicks.description: Where the copy starts, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). The copy always lands on the SOURCE clip's own track — this command carries no destination track — so that span must be clear.

tools.name: studio_clip_duplicate

tools.description: Move a batch of notes in time and/or pitch (the piano-roll drag). The engine does NOT clamp: if the batch would move any note out of range the WHOLE command is refused with a typed error and nothing is applied. Clamping here would break self-inversion (clamp then negate the delta does not return the original) and would collapse a chord onto the boundary note by note; group-clamping that preserves voicing is the caller's job.

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. One chord drag is ONE journal entry, so relative offsets inside the selection are a property of the command rather than the caller's responsibility.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

Clamping here would break self-inversion (clamp then negate the delta does not return the original) and would collapse a chord onto the boundary note by note; group-clamping that preserves voicing is the caller's job.

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

deltaPitch.description: Signed semitone offset applied to the copies, -127 to 127. No clamping: if any copy would leave 0..127 the whole command is refused.

newNoteIds.description: Ids for the copies, positionally paired with noteIds and the same length. Minted UI-side.

tools.description: Set the ABSOLUTE start and length of a batch of notes. The one note command that is not delta-shaped, and it exists for exactly one reason: an inverse that has to restore per-note positions no single delta describes. note.quantize names it as its inverse. Self-inverse because the inverse is the same command carrying the pre-state values, the clip.move pattern. Pitch and velocity are untouched: this command is about TIME only, so it can never silently retune a chord.

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

notes.description: One entry per note. Every noteId must be distinct and must already exist in the clip.

lengthTicks.description: Absolute sounding length in ticks, not a delta. Must be > 0.

noteId.description: An EXISTING note in this clip. This command never creates or removes a note; note.add / note.remove own that.

startTicks.description: Absolute clip-relative position, not a delta.

tools.name: studio_note_timing_set

tools.description: Pull a batch of notes toward a grid at a given strength. NEVER automatic: nothing in the engine issues this on capture, on import or on load, because the point of a tempo-mapped recording is that the grid was fitted to the performance rather than the other way round. NOT self-inverse and not a delta command: every note moves by its own amount, so the inverse is one note.timing.set carrying the EXACT prior start and length of every note in the batch. Refused whole (nothing applied) if any note would land before tick 0 or, with quantizeEnds, be squeezed below one tick.

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

gridTicks.description: The grid division to pull toward, in ticks (960 = a quarter at PPQ 960, 240 = a sixteenth). Lines are measured from the project's phaseAnchorTicks, so a song with a lead-in quantizes to its real bar 1 rather than to tick 0.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. REQUIRED and non-empty: there is deliberately no "quantize the whole clip" spelling, because quantize is destructive to a performance that was played off the grid on purpose. A caller that means every note enumerates every note.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

quantizeEnds.description: false: only note STARTS move, lengths are preserved exactly. true: the note END is pulled to the same grid at the same strength, so lengths change. Off is the musical default; legato passages get chopped by an ends-quantize.

strengthPercent.description: How far each note travels toward its grid line, as an INTEGER percent. 100 is mechanical; 50-80 tightens the timing while keeping the feel. Integer rather than a 0..1 float because journaled values are Num and the hash chain depends on their integer/float shape (0.8 and 80 are not interchangeable under canonicalization).

visible.description: true would show the lane, false hide it. NOT IMPLEMENTED in the engine: the command validates trackId and target and returns ok with mutated:false, storing nothing — the Studio UI keeps lane visibility in its own view state, so calling this over the agent surface moves nothing on screen and nothing reads the flag back.

positionTicks.description: Where the point sits, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

trackId.description: Id of the track that owns the lane.

trackId.description: Id of the track that owns the lane.

tools.description: Set a track's mixer channel gain (distinct from clip.setGain, which trims an individual clip).

tools.description: Append an effect to the insert chain on a track, a bus/group node, or master. A SEPARATE registry from device.add, whose 'kind' enum is NOT widened: build_instrument hard-errors on a track with more than one device, so an effect in Track.devices would break the compile of every instrument track that also carries an effect. Its parameters become automatable IMMEDIATELY through track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> / bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> / master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> - no catalog schema change, because the autopoint/autolane target pattern already admits them. A NEW command name (E0 9.2).

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

kind.description: Which effect to insert, from the CLOSED E5 vocabulary: 'eq', 'compressor', 'gate', 'delay', 'reverb', 'saturator', 'chorus', 'utility' or 'limiter'. An unknown kind fails loudly at the contract boundary rather than building a silent no-op node.

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

tools.name: studio_fx_add

tools.description: Remove an effect from an insert chain. Undo restores the effect, its chain index, every stored parameter and its sidechain link - a multi-command inverse; the catalog hint is the declared fx.add. Unlike device.remove this refuses nothing for stored parameters: fx.param.set can restore them, so the guard device.remove needs would only make every configured effect unremovable. Refused only if the effect carries unknown fields no command in this build can restore.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

tools.name: studio_fx_remove

tools.description: Reorder one effect within its insert chain. Self-inverse: the inverse carries the prior index, and remove+insert is a rotation whose reverse restores exactly.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

index.description: New 0-based position in the chain. Chain order IS processing order.

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

tools.name: studio_fx_move

tools.description: Set one effect parameter. Parameters stay SPARSE: an absent key means the DSP default, exactly as build_instrument already implements it, so no default is ever materialized into the project. inverseShape is 'multi' because the declared inverse name cannot cover both directions - the real inverse is a fx.param.set carrying the prior value, OR a fx.param.clear when the key was absent, so an undo returns the key to ABSENT rather than to a written default. This is the parameter setter E1/E2 deliberately omitted for Device; E5 is the DSP lane and can supply the semantics E1/E2 could not.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

key.description: An effect parameter key from FX_PARAM_KEYS. Which keys a given kind honours is deliberately NOT validated: apply.rs runs on replay, so tightening the (kind, key) pairing later would break replay of a project that automated a key its kind ignores. A lane bound to an ignored key is surfaced by CompileReport.inert_lanes instead.

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

value.description: Parameter value. Journaled as a Num, so the integer/float SHAPE round-trips exactly.

tools.name: studio_fx_param_set

tools.description: Drop one stored effect parameter, restoring sparsity so the key reads as the DSP default again. Clearing a key that stores no value is a typed error, not a silent no-op: a no-op has no exact inverse to journal.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

key.description: An effect parameter key from FX_PARAM_KEYS. target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

tools.description: Key an effect's detector from another node. A sidechain is an ORDERING CONSTRAINT, not an audio edge: it creates no routing edge and contributes no audio, but the source must be scheduled before the host or the detector reads a not-yet-written accumulator - exactly 0.0, i.e. silence, not a small error. Rejected at command time if the source does not resolve, is the host itself (that is the internal detector, not a link), is master, or would create a cycle over edges and links together. inverseShape is 'multi' because the inverse is a set-to-prior OR a clear.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

tools.name: studio_fx_sidechain_set

tools.description: Return an effect's detector to its internal (self) key. Clearing an effect that has no link is a typed error, not a silent no-op.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

regionStartTicks.description: Region start in project ticks, on the bar-snapped beat-tracked grid (read ppq and tempoMap from studio_snapshot to convert bars to ticks; the grid origin is phaseAnchorTicks, which is not always 0).

tools.name: studio_audition

tools.description: Commit a chosen variant: promote its take(s) into their clip(s) as ONE undo transaction, the crossfade already baked into each spliced asset. Pass the variant's promotions from studio_revise.

promotions.description: The chosen variant's promotions (from studio_revise variantTakes).

clipId.description: The clip that take is spliced into — one entry per scoped stem clip.

takeId.description: The candidate take to promote, as studio_revise reported it in variantTakes.

tools.name: studio_commit

tools.description: The draft/commit two-phase: re-render committed draft take(s) at the commit rung (base-50) and swap each clip's asset draft->full as ONE undo transaction. Reconstructs region + crossfade from journaled provenance, so it needs only the draft take ids. Sample-aligned and undoable.

draftTakeIds.description: The committed draft takes to finalize.

engine.description: mock (deterministic fixture, default) or live (needs a Gen Node).

tools.name: studio_finalize

tools.description: Discard an audition without committing: the takes stay as candidates in the Takes history (purging them is the Takes browser's job).

takeIds.description: Optional take ids from the audition being abandoned; they are echoed back as kept. Omitted discards nothing and simply reports an empty set — the takes survive either way, because nothing was committed.

tools.name: studio_discard

tools.description: Extend a clip past its end (01-DESIGN 3.3): generate variant tails as candidate takes. Commit the chosen tail with studio_commit_extend (crossfaded at the seam, new section).

clipId.description: The clip to extend past its end; the new audio is butt-joined at its tail.

crossfadeMs.description: Optional seam crossfade length in milliseconds, 5 ms declick floor. Default 20 ms.

engine.description: mock (deterministic fixture, default) or live (needs a Gen Node).

instruction.description: Optional, e.g. '16-bar outro, decays to vinyl noise'.

seed.description: Optional base seed; each variant derives its own from it. Omitted uses a fixed built-in base, so a repeat call reproduces the same tails.

variants.description: How many alternative tails to generate, 1 to 8. Default 1.

tools.name: studio_extend

tools.description: Place a chosen extend tail as a new clip butt-joined at the seam, crossfade the seam, and add a section, as ONE undo transaction.

clipId.description: The clip being extended (the seam anchor).

crossfadeMs.description: Optional seam crossfade length in milliseconds, 5 ms declick floor. Default 20 ms.

sectionName.description: Optional label for the arrangement section the tail becomes. Default 'Extension'.

takeId.description: The chosen tail take from studio_extend.

tools.name: studio_commit_extend

tools.description: Add a Layer (01-DESIGN 3.3b, lego): generate a new instrument that fits a context region, as candidate takes. Commit with studio_commit_layer to land it on a NEW track.

contextClipId.description: Optional context clip the layer should fit.

engine.description: mock (deterministic fixture, default) or live (needs a Gen Node).

instruction.description: The instrument, e.g. 'warm analog bass', 'sax lead answering the vocal'.

regionEndTicks.description: End of the context region in project ticks, exclusive. Must be greater than regionStartTicks.

regionStartTicks.description: Start of the context region the layer has to fit, in project ticks. Read ppq and phaseAnchorTicks from studio_snapshot to convert bars to ticks.

seed.description: Optional base seed; each variant derives its own from it. Omitted uses a fixed built-in base, so a repeat call reproduces the same layers.

stem.description: The stem lane the layer reads as (default other).

targetTrackId.description: Optional id for the NEW track the layer lands on; it is created by this call. Omitted mints one ('trk_layer_<ulid>').

variants.description: How many alternative layers to generate, 1 to 8. Default 1.

tools.name: studio_layer

tools.description: Create a new track and place a chosen layer take on it at the region, as ONE undo transaction.

color.description: Optional track colour as '#RRGGBB' hex. Omitted uses the stem's standard colour.

regionStartTicks.description: Where the layer clip is placed, in project ticks — normally the same region start studio_layer was given.

takeId.description: The chosen layer take from studio_layer.

targetTrackId.description: Optional id of the track studio_layer already created. Omitted mints a new one.

trackName.description: Optional display name for the new track. Default 'Layer'.

tools.name: studio_commit_layer

tools.description: Undo the most recent undo unit (journaled forward; history never rewrites).
tools.name: studio_undo

tools.description: Redo the most recently undone unit.
tools.name: studio_redo

tools.description: Set the metronome's monitor state: turn the click on or off, set how loud it is, and start an audible count-in. The click is a synthesised transient on every beat, accented on the downbeat, locked to the project tempo map and phase anchor. It is MONITOR-ONLY: you hear it while you play, and it can never appear in an exported mix or in a recorded take. Nothing here is journaled or undoable.

countInBeats.description: Sound this many count-in clicks starting NOW, accented on the first, whether or not the transport is rolling. 0 cancels a count-in in progress.

enabled.description: Turn the click on or off. Same state as transport.metronome.

levelDb.description: Click level relative to the default, in dB. 0 is the default level (-12 dBFS peak).

tools.name: studio_metronome_set

tools.description: Sound one note on a track's instrument RIGHT NOW, outside the timeline (a piano-roll key, an on-screen key, a MIDI key). The note itself is not journaled and not undoable: this is feedback, not an edit. Omit trackId to play the project's instrument, creating one if the project has none (that creation IS journaled, as one undo step). Opens the output device only on a host whose GUI opted into audible output; on a headless host or under test it returns audible:false with a reason and makes no sound.

gate.description: oneShot (default) releases itself after holdMs; on holds until a matching off (a held key).

pitch.description: MIDI note number, 0 to 127; 60 is middle C.

trackId.description: The instrument track to sound. Omit to use the armed instrument track, else the first, else a newly created one.

velocity.description: How hard the key is struck, 0 to 127. Optional, default 100.

tools.name: studio_note_preview

tools.description: Keep what was just played. Everything played on an instrument is held in a bounded rolling buffer whether or not anything was armed or recording; this lands that buffer as real notes in one undoable step. Read snapshot.performance.keepableNotes to see how much is there. Refuses while a record.start take is open — stop that take instead.
tools.name: studio_performance_keep

tools.description: Throw away what was just played, WITHOUT putting any of it in the project. The counterpart of studio_performance_keep: it empties the rolling retro-capture buffer and nothing else. It cannot touch a clip, a note or a take, journals nothing, and is therefore not undoable — there is nothing for an undo to restore. Refuses while a record.start take is open; use record.cancel for that.
tools.name: studio_performance_discard
